NEW PATIENT VISIT

66M retired letter carrier transferring care; prior PCP retired this summer. Brought his bottles in a grocery bag. Feels fine, here mostly to get set up and get refills somewhere reliable.

PMH
- HTN, roughly 12 yrs. On lisinopril 20. Says readings at the pharmacy kiosk are usually "in the 140s."
- T2DM since about 2016, metformin only. Last A1c he remembers was "around 7 and a half."
- Hyperlipidemia, atorvastatin 40 for about 10 yrs.
- Former smoker: 30 pack-yrs, quit in August, cold turkey. No patches or gum. Proud of it, says the cravings are mostly gone after meals now.

PSH: lap chole 2005; L inguinal hernia repair 2012.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Reconciled against bottles.
Allergies: NKDA.

FHx: father MI at 61. Mother T2DM. Brother had an ischemic stroke at 65.

SHx: retired after 30-some years delivering mail. Lives in Williamsburg. Beer or two a week, sometimes none. No drugs. Drives.

ROS negative for chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, claudication, polyuria, vision change, numbness in feet.

Exam: vitals as charted, BP above goal. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no bruits. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, well-healed lap chole port scars, L groin scar. No edema. Feet: intact monofilament bilaterally, pulses 2+, skin intact.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P
1. HTN, above goal on lisinopril 20. Continue for now; recheck at next visit with kiosk log.
2. T2DM. A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin. Eye exam due; he'll call his optometrist.
3. Hyperlipidemia. Lipids today, continue atorvastatin 40.
4. Tobacco: nicotine dependence, in remission since August. Encouraged. Eligible for annual low-dose CT; discussed what it is and false-positive rate, he wants it. Ordered.
5. Health maintenance: flu high-dose and updated COVID given today. Hep C and HIV screen with labs. Records requested from prior PCP for colonoscopy and vaccine history.

RTC 3 months.

documents.body: Hi Mr. Kaminski, your labs from Tuesday are back. Kidney and liver tests and blood counts are normal, and the urine protein test is normal. Your A1c is a bit above 7, which is close to where we'd like it, so no changes for now. Cholesterol is higher than ideal; we'll keep working on it. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. documents.body:
CC: heart "fluttering"

HPI: 68M with HTN, T2DM, HLD, ex-smoker. Since around mid-June has noticed episodes of his heart racing and skipping, some lasting most of an afternoon. A bit winded carrying the hose up the slope to the garden, which is new for him. Denies chest pain, lightheadedness or passing out. No caffeine change, no new meds or supplements. Alcohol unchanged, a beer or two weekly.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. NKDA.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 98 and irregularly irregular, SpO2 97% RA. Comfortable. JVP flat. Heart irregular, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. No leg edema.

ECG in office: AF, rate 100, no acute ST changes.
Labs drawn today, results back this afternoon: Hgb 14.2, plt 250, INR 1.0, Cr 1.1. TSH and A1c pending.

A/P
1. Atrial fibrillation, new, unknown duration but symptoms ~2 months. Rate under 110 at rest and he is stable, so no rate drug started today. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (HTN, DM, age 65-74), annual stroke risk meaningfully elevated. Recommended apixaban 5 mg BID; went over bleeding risk vs stroke risk and his brother's stroke. He does not want to be on a blood thinner right now and would like to talk to a heart doctor first. Respect that; will revisit. TSH today. Echo ordered. Cardiology referral placed. Return precautions: chest pain, fainting, sustained fast heartbeat, any weakness/numbness/speech change - call 911.
2. HTN - 142/88, continue lisinopril 20.
3. T2DM - A1c pending, continue metformin.
4. HLD - continue atorvastatin 40.

Total time 50 min.

documents.title: Thyroid and other results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Kaminski, your thyroid test is normal, so that isn't the cause of the irregular heartbeat. A1c is about the same as your last few. Echo is booked for the 27th and the cardiology office will call you with a date. The offer on the blood thinner stands any time you want to talk about it again.

documents.title: Cardiology consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outpatient cardiology consultation

Thank you for referring Mr. Kaminski, 68, for atrial fibrillation found at your office on 8/14.

He reports intermittent palpitations since early summer. Since your visit he has felt a few shorter spells, none in the past week. No chest discomfort, presyncope or syncope.

History: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia, former smoker (30 pack-years, quit 2023). Cholecystectomy, inguinal hernia repair.
Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: father MI at 61, brother stroke at 65.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Regular rhythm today, no murmur, lungs clear, no edema.

ECG today: sinus rhythm 72, normal intervals.
Echo 8/27: LVEF 60%, normal LA size, no significant valve disease.
TSH normal per your records.

Impression: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, structurally normal heart. CHA2DS2-VASc 3.

Recommendations:
1. Oral anticoagulation recommended: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (no dose-reduction criteria). We discussed this at length. He understands his stroke risk and declines anticoagulation for now. He knows he can change his mind at any time.
2. No rate or rhythm drug at present given infrequent, tolerable episodes and sinus rhythm today.
3. Seek emergency care for sustained rapid palpitations, chest pain, fainting or stroke symptoms.
4. Follow-up in cardiology in 4 months.

Sincerely,
Outpatient Cardiology

reports.text: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular rate, approximately 170. Narrow QRS. No ST-segment elevation or depression. No T-wave inversion.
reports.conclusion: Atrial fibrillation, rapid ventricular rate. No ischemic changes.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 82. Normal intervals. No ST-T abnormality.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD (received 10/14/2025)
Date of service: 10/12/2025

CC: palpitations, short of breath

HPI: 68-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes and paroxysmal AF diagnosed this August, not anticoagulated, who was raking out garden beds about two hours before arrival when his heart started pounding and he became short of breath. Has not let up. Denies chest pain, near-fainting or fainting.

PMH: HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia, paroxysmal AF, former smoker.
Meds: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Allergies: NKDA.

Triage: BP 90/60, HR 170, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air.
Exam: anxious, alert, speaking full sentences. Neck veins not distended. Tachycardic and irregular. Lungs clear, no rales. No peripheral edema. Neuro nonfocal.

ECG: AF with RVR ~170, narrow complex, no ST or T-wave abnormality.
Labs: WBC 7.5, Hgb 14, Plt 250. Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 1.0, glucose 180.

Course: Hypotensive with rapid AF, onset clearly under 48 hours. Procedural sedation, synchronized cardioversion, single 200 J biphasic shock, converted to sinus. Post-procedure BP 124/76, HR 82 sinus. Recovered from sedation without event and was walking around the department.

Anticoagulation: CHA2DS2-VASc 3. Advised apixaban, including the recommended period after cardioversion. Patient declined after discussion; capacity intact; understands risk of stroke. He will follow up with his cardiologist.

Impression: paroxysmal AF with RVR and hypotension, cardioverted to sinus rhythm.
Disposition: home in stable condition at 21:30. PCP follow-up within the week, cardiology follow-up as scheduled. Return for recurrent palpitations, chest pain, fainting, weakness or speech trouble.

Emergency Medicine attending

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY - Stroke Service
Admitted 07/04/2026, discharged 07/08/2026

Discharge diagnosis: acute lacunar infarct, right posterior limb of internal capsule.
Other: paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; hypertension; type 2 diabetes; hyperlipidemia; former smoker.

Presentation: abrupt left face, arm and leg weakness (3/5) with intact sensation; BP 180/95 on arrival. Outside the thrombolysis window. Head CT without hemorrhage or mass effect.

Hospital course:
- MRI: 12 mm acute infarct in the right posterior limb of the internal capsule, no hemorrhage.
- Carotid duplex: no significant stenosis.
- Telemetry: sinus rhythm throughout.
- Fasting lipids 7/5: TC 220, HDL 35, LDL 160, TG 250. Atorvastatin increased to 80 mg.
- Echo in August 2025 was normal; not repeated.
- Anticoagulation: CHA2DS2-VASc now 5. After discussion with patient, who now agrees, apixaban 5 mg twice daily started on hospital day 4 (07/07) given small infarct size.
- BP: permissive for 48 hours, then lisinopril resumed and amlodipine 5 mg added.
- PT/OT: improving; safe for home with outpatient therapy.

Exam at discharge: left lower facial weakness, left arm and leg 4-/5, sensation intact, walking with standby assist.

Discharge medications:
- apixaban 5 mg twice daily (NEW)
- atorvastatin 80 mg daily (CHANGED from 40 mg)
- amlodipine 5 mg daily (NEW)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- metformin 1000 mg twice daily
Allergies: NKDA

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; stroke neurology clinic in 6 weeks; outpatient PT/OT referral sent. Repeat lipids in 6-8 weeks.

Stroke Service attending

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital f/u, discharge summary and ED record reviewed.

Admitted 7/4-7/8 for a right internal capsule lacunar infarct, presenting with left face/arm/leg weakness. Not thrombolysed (outside window). Started apixaban 7/7, atorvastatin up to 80, amlodipine 5 added.

Today: left hand still clumsy with buttons, leg feels heavy by evening. No new weakness, no headache. Taking every dose of apixaban; using a pill box. No bleeding or bruising. Mood ok, a bit shaken. Not driving.

Meds reconciled: apixaban 5 BID, atorvastatin 80, amlodipine 5, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID. NKDA.

Exam: BP 138/82. Regular rhythm. Mild left lower facial asymmetry. Left arm 4/5, left leg 4/5. Sensation intact. Walks without a device, slightly slow on the left.

A/P
1. Lacunar stroke, right internal capsule. Improving. Outpatient PT/OT starting 7/21. Neurology 8/18.
2. Paroxysmal AF, now on apixaban. Full dose appropriate (age under 80, weight over 60 kg, Cr ~1). BMP today.
3. HTN: 138/82 on lisinopril + new amlodipine. Goal under 130/80; recheck at next visit before adjusting.
4. HLD: atorvastatin 80; lipids and LFTs in 6 weeks.
5. T2DM: continue metformin.

Outpatient Physical Therapy - Initial Evaluation
Date: 07/21/2026
Referral: stroke service, left hemiparesis after lacunar infarct.

Subjective: left leg tires with longer walks; left hand fine motor slower.
Objective: left hip flexion and knee extension 4/5, ankle dorsiflexion 4/5. Left grip reduced compared with right. Gait independent without device, mildly decreased left step length. Static and dynamic standing balance good.
Assessment: mild left-sided weakness after stroke, good rehab potential.
Plan: 2x/week for 8 weeks, strengthening, gait and balance training, home exercise program. OT for fine motor running alongside.
Precautions: on anticoagulant.

documents.title: Stroke clinic follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Stroke Neurology Clinic

Mr. Kaminski returns 6 weeks after a right internal capsule lacunar infarct. He has been doing PT and OT twice weekly and notes steady gains; buttons are easier. No new neurologic symptoms. Taking apixaban twice daily, atorvastatin 80 and amlodipine. No bleeding.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Alert, fluent. Faint left nasolabial flattening. Left arm 4+/5, left leg 4+/5. Sensation normal. Gait steady.

Assessment: lacunar stroke with good recovery of left-sided weakness; paroxysmal AF now anticoagulated.

Recommendations:
1. Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily long term.
2. Continue atorvastatin 80 mg. LDL goal under 70; please repeat lipids now.
3. BP goal under 130/80, per PCP.
4. Continue PT/OT to complete course.
5. Return to neurology in 6 months.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.
Stroke Neurology
